lessonObjective: Help parents understand how giving children appropriate choices develops confidence, responsibility and resilience.
learningOutcomes: Understand why choice is essential for healthy child development
Recognise the difference between guidance and control
Identify age-appropriate decisions children can make
Develop a plan to increase responsibility at home

sections.title: Choice Reflection
instructions: List five decisions you made for your child today
List five decisions your child made independently
discussionQuestions: Are you surprised by the balance?
Where might your child be ready for more responsibility?

content.facilitatorNotes: Children who never make decisions often become dependent on adults. Appropriate choices encourage judgement and confidence.

sections.title: Choice and Self-Esteem
sections.activity: Participants reflect on a childhood decision they were trusted to make.

sections.title: Jack
sections.scenario: Eight-year-old Jack refuses to choose clothes, activities or meals because adults always decide for him.
questions: What skills might Jack be missing?
What message may Jack have learned about himself?
How could responsibility be gradually transferred?

sections.title: Implementation Planning
tasks: One choice to introduce within a month

homework.task: Introduce three age-appropriate choices during the week

reflection: What am I afraid might happen if I let go?
What would greater independence look like in six months?
